rows.what the ink shows: The deleted line retains two deep lower loops under the early and middle word groups, a comma-like drop after the middle group, and raised dots plus a final upright near the right end. The heavy continuous cancellation merges the intervening letter bodies, so these remnants do not establish the full proposed word sequence.

Between the erased equals sign and the first tensor sign is one tall, nearly straight numeral stem with a short basal foot. It stands on the formula baseline and is distinct from the neighboring circular tensor sign.

The lower canceled phrase preserves short initial uprights, a long descending loop in the middle and an upright with a low terminal hook at the right, while cancellation covers its small letter bodies. A second canceled upper run begins with a tall looped capital-like stroke; its relation to the lower phrase is not securely separable, so neither the entire wording nor the layer allocation is resolved.

The short word between the comma and F_i has a small left loop, a tall narrow stroke near its left middle, and two low bumps fused into a dark horizontal band. The fused bodies do not distinguish the letters required for avec.

At the lower right of the single baseline E, the deletion line cuts between an upper angular bend and a lower hook. Those could be connected parts of 2, but the covered junction also prevents excluding a 1 with a separate overwritten upper stroke; the nearby parenthesized 2 over the tensor sign is a distinct layer.

The deleted word after on has a rounded left remnant, a dark central upright and an exit stroke that bends down at the right. Dense overwriting and a brown patch conceal the inner bodies and the proposed p/e/u/t separation.

Inside the final norm there is one baseline A with two diagonal legs and a crossbar, one separate raised t at its upper left with a small cross stroke and hooked return, and one lower-right index 1. The raised letter is visibly present, excluding the candidate with A_1 alone.

The first word has a tall P with an upper bowl followed by a low a body and terminal r shoulder. The second starts with a compact s hook, runs through the low u/i sequence with a separate dot, and ends in a crossed t and short e return.

One baseline u has a distinct short lowered 1, followed by a ring with an oblique crossing. The continuation lies on the deletion rule: dot positions are merged into it and the final ring retains its lower oval but no separable diagonal cross; the raised (3) belongs to the inserted line above, not this formula.

A small loop at the left, several low rises, and a larger central oval remain visible above a thick zigzag cancellation. The intervening letter joins and ending are covered, so these remnants do not establish all of continue.

The small two-part s-loop and tall looped terminal f survive the horizontal cancellation; its tiny exit upturn is followed by a blank gap, with no o-r-m-e bodies or abbreviation dot. The preceding tall t-like stroke and covered low joins leave the prefix tran uncertain, while the visible ending is sf.

A large looped initial R and a low wave with one deep descending turn survive, followed by a faint tall stroke and small curved forms. The pale bodies and a further separated right cluster with two ascenders leave wording and cluster allocation uncertain; retaining the source candidate does not assert complete wording or a two-word count.

The cancelled baseline retains an initial rising stroke, a detached dot, scattered uprights and small loops below the heavy rule. Most word bodies and their divisions are submerged; the clear Soit maintenant belongs to the higher inserted line and does not establish the erased wording.

After the cancelled Posons, a shallow initial hook and several narrow rising tips project above a thick horizontal cancellation, ending in a hooked trailing stroke. The covered lower bodies do not distinguish the n-c-o-r-e sequence sufficiently.

The left remnant has a tall upright and curved foot, while the right retains several upright or descending strokes and a separate dot. Two heavy cancellation passes cover the intervening bodies and joins, preventing a secure reading of either un or proj.
The compact joined word ends in an a-i-t sequence with a single short detached dot-stroke over the i and a rising terminal t. There is no two-sided circumflex over that vowel.

notes: Source image measured 1675 x 2158 pixels. No OCR, recognition, ImageGen or external transcription used.
M1181, M1183, M1184 and M1186 retain uncertainty after detailed inspection because cancellation obscures distinguishing bodies. M1185 index remains uncertain at the crossed layer junction.
M1183 upper canceled run has unresolved allocation; it is not asserted to be an outside-span error. Independent layer check was requested from the coordinator.
All listed views were actually inspected; no rotation was applied. The primary interval includes report preparation and coordination between visual views.

Peer reconciliation, M1183: work/scan060_peer.json independently distinguishes the two canceled textual baselines, but the upper inscription remains unallocated and no outside-span error is accepted. The peer secures terminal les; my previously viewed crops establish its tall initial and terminal hook, while I did not securely separate all of the low e/s bodies from cancellation. I therefore retain the broader original uncertainty. This is an annotation-only reconciliation, with no new view or reading change; the primary finish and initial report remain unchanged.
